title: Final Decision Settlement Agreement C26-0006 Case 2025BS09 P G WITHERNAY Ms Lucy ROBINSON
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY THE FEI TRIBUNAL
9 July 2026
In the matter of
FÉDÉRATION EQUESTRE INTERNATIONALE (the “FEI”)
vs.
Ms. Lucy ROBINSON –Person Responsible (the “PR”)
together the “Parties”
(Reference No. FEI Tribunal: C26-0006 ROBINSON)
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Ms. Diane Pitts, (USA), Sole Panel Member
FEI Case number: 2025/BS09 P G WITHERNAY - Ms. Lucy ROBINSON (GBR)
Horse/Passport: P G WITHERNAY/106NI31/GBR
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Lucy ROBINSON/10107550/GBR
Event/Date: CCI3*-L - Hartpury (GBR), 05 – 10.08.2025
Event/ID: 2025_CI_0671_C_S_02
Date of sample collection: 09.08.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Trazodone
Bar Code No.: 1608754
1

All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not otherwise defined
herein shall have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the FEI General
Regulations (the “GRs”) and Statutes (the” Statutes”), the FEI Veterinary Regulations (the
“VRs”), the 2025 Equine Prohibited Substance List and the Equine Anti-Doping and
Controlled Medication Regulations (the “EADCMRs”). The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the
“EADRs” or “EAD Rules”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the “ECMRs” or “ECM
Rules”) are set out in the EADCMRs.
I. Introduction
1. This Decision pertains to the FEI case 2025/BS09 2025/BS09 P G WITHERNAY. In this
matter, the FEI notified the PR of a violation of Article 2.1 (The Presence of a Banned
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) of the EAD Rules. This
violation was based on the positive finding of Trazodone in the Sample of the Horse
P G WITHERNAY (the “Horse”) which was collected at the CCI3*-L - Hartpury (GBR),
05 – 10.08.2025 (the “Event”).
2. The FEI and the PR agreed to a Settlement Agreement on 23 March 2026 (the
“Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement together with the attached
Exhibits are hereby incorporated by reference in this Decision.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions
3. The following regulations are applicable to the present case:
Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023.
General Regulations, 24thedition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January 2025.
Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (the “IRs”).
FEI Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations, 4th edition, effective
1 January 2025.
FEI Veterinary Regulations, 15th edition 2023, effective 1 January 2025.
III. Factual background and initial proceedings
2

4. Ms Lucy ROBINSON (FEI ID 10107550) is a rider in the discipline of Eventing1 and
the PR in accordance with Article 118.3 of the GRs. She competed with the Horse at
the Event. The PR is a member of the British Equestrian Federation (the “GBR-NF”),
the latter being a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EADRs.
5. The FEI is the sole IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian
sport disciplines of Dressage and Para-Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and
Para-Driving, Endurance and Vaulting.
6. At the Event, on 9 August 2025, during the cross-country phase, the PR submitted
that the Horse suffered a serious fall. She explained that the Horse was treated on
course with pain relief and sedation and was transported by horse ambulance to
the onsite equine hospital for further investigation. It was also submitted that at
approximately 17:15 on the same day, the PR was informed that the injuries to the
Horse were so severe that the only humane option was euthanasia and as such the
Horse was euthanised.
7. Due to the fatality of the Horse at this Event, the Horse was further tested on 9
August 2025. Blood samples (Sample no 1608754) were collected from the Horse
and sent to the FEI approved Laboratory, LGC Newmarket Road, Fordham,
Cambridgeshire (GBR) (the “Laboratory”), for analysis. The analysis of the blood
sample revealed the presence of Trazodone; an antidepressant used in the
treatment of depression and anxiety in humans. is classified as a Banned
Substance, which is prohibited at all times, under the FEI Equine Prohibited
Substances List.2
8. The positive finding of Trazodone in the Sample therefore gave rise to a violation of
the EAD Rules (the “EAD Rule Violation”).
9. The FEI informed the PR of the EAD Rule Violation in a notification letter dated 23
September 2025 (the “Notification Letter”). In accordance with Article 7.4.1. of the
EAD Rules, the FEI provisionally suspended the PR as of the date of the Notification
Letter (the “Provisional Suspension”).
1 Please note it originally stated in the Settlement Agreement that Ms. Lucy ROBINSON (FEI ID: 10107550), the Person
Responsible (“PR”) in accordance with Article 118.3 of the FEI General Regulations, is a show jumping rider competing for Great
Britain however she is a PR in the discipline of Eventing.
2 2025 FEI Equine Prohibited Substances List.
https://inside.fei.org/sites/default/files/2025%20Prohibited%20Substances%20List.pdf
3

10. The PR had the right to request an analysis of the B Sample. The Owner of the Horse
requested the B Sample analysis on 29 September 2025.The B Sample analysis of
the blood sample confirmed the presence of Trazodone. The PR was notified of the
results of the B Sample testing by letter dated 27 October 2025.
11. In the Notification Letter, the FEI further informed the PR of her right to provide an
explanation within 20 days from the date of the Notification Letter.
12. The PR submitted her written explanations on 24 November 2025, supplemented
by additional evidence on 26 and 28 January 2026, which were as follows:
a. The Horse was prescribed Sucralfate powder by a veterinarian to be
administered in the morning feed in order to treat the Horse’s gastric ulcers;
b. In June 2025, the PR visited the Owners of the Horse (together with the Horse)
as she was offered to have a training session with the previous trainer of this
Horse (who is also a family friend of the Owners). The PR stayed on their farm
one night and she took with her the prescribed medication, Sucralfate as well
as the Horse’s feed, hay and all other equipment;
c. The PR left the Owners farm on 27 June 2025 where she forgot and left
behind the Horse’s medication Sucralfate. The PR was not worried about it as
she had another tub of this medication at home;
d. The Sucralfate container was returned by the Owners to the PR on 27 July
2025 i.e., one month later, and as of that day the PR started to use the
medication from the returned container;
e. The Horse underwent the doping control sampling at the Event on 9 August
2025;
f. Following the notice of the Rule violation, it was discovered that a person that
helped the Owners with their other horses (the “Helper”), contaminated the
Sucralfate medication with Trazodone while it was left at the Owner’s farm
(and when the PR had already left). Another horse of the Owner, BELINDA,
was prescribed Trazodone by a veterinarian; when preparing the meal for
BELINDA, the Helper measured a dose of Trazodone but as it was not enough,
the Helper topped it up with the Sucralfate medication that was stored in the
medical cabinet (assuming that it was the same medication as Trazodone as
the containers looked the same). The Helper then put the spoon that she
used (from Trazodone medication) in the container of Sucralfate;
g. The PR submitted expert opinion of Dr Emmanuel Strahm stating that “the
measured level of trazodone contamination in the Sucralfate is fully consistent
with the blood concentration detected in the Horse. Dr. Strahm concludes that the
contamination scenario is highly probable and adequately accounts for the
laboratory findings.” ;
4

h. The PR provided additional supporting evidence and documents in order to
corroborate her explanations, namely:
- Medical records of the Horse P G WITHERNAY, confirming the medical
condition of gastric ulcers and the prescribed treatment with the
medication Sucralfate;
- Medical records of the other leisure Horse Belinda and the prescribed
medication Trazodone;
- Lab analysis of the unopened medication of Sucralfate (which tested
negative to Trazodone);
- Lab analysis of the Sucralfate medication used by the PR (which tested
positive to Trazodone);
- Lab analysis of various products and supplements used by the PR – all of
those products tested negative to Trazodone;
- Dr Strahm Opinion Letter confirming the scientific plausibility of the
provided explanations by the PR;
- Testimonies of the PR, the Owner and the trainer which all confirm the
occurrence of the above-mentioned events;
- Testimony of the Helper who mixed up the two medications;
- Pictures of the packages of the two medications, the spoon and the
powders themselves (which appear easy to mix up if one does not read
the label).
i. Consequently, Trazodone detected in the Horse’s Sample, more likely than
not came from the medication Sucralfate that was inadvertently
contaminated by the Helper when preparing the meal for the Horse BELINDA.
This came to the PR’s and Owner’s attention only after the PR received the FEI
Notification Letter of 23 September 2025. As such, the PR bears No Fault or
Negligence (or, in the alternative, No Significant Fault or Negligence) for the
presence of Trazodone in the Horse’s sample.
13. In order to verify the provided explanations, the FEI consulted its external scientific
expert as to whether those explanations, as compared to the concentration of
Trazodone detected in the Horse’s Sample, are scientifically plausible and whether
the provided explanations could indeed be the source of the positive finding. The
FEI expert confirmed that those explanations are indeed scientifically plausible.
14. The FEI therefore agreed that the PR’s explanation of the source was consistent with
the Adverse Analytical Finding in the Horse, and was therefore satisfied that the PR
has established, on a balance of probabilities, how Trazodone entered the Horse’s
system.
5

15. Fault and Negligence for the rule violation- In evaluating the PR’s level of fault or
negligence, if any, for the Rule Violation under Art. 2.1 of the EADRs, the FEI took
into account in particular the following considerations:
- Neither the PR, nor the Owner of the Horse were aware of the
contamination of the Sucralfate medication by the Helper before they
received the FEI Notification Letter dated 23 September 2025. The PR used
the returned Sucralfate medication in good faith and did not suspect at
any point that it could have been contaminated with a Prohibited
Substance by a third person as there were no obvious external signs that
the Sucralfate has been tampered with;
- The PR was well aware of her antidoping obligations and her general
approach to horse management shows a high standard of care, both, at
home stables and at competitions;
- On the other hand, the FEI noted that under anti-doping jurisprudence,
the CAS strictly maintains that athletes who fail to secure their medications
– leaving it without supervision or not “under lock” – cannot establish a
plea of No Fault or Negligence as they did not exercise the “utmost
caution”.;
- In the case of CAS 2005/A/951, Canas v. ATP, the CAS Panel held that “a
player is being clearly negligent when relying blindly on the system set up to
take care of him at a Tournament site, assuming that it is foolproof. The player
has a duty of utmost caution after visiting the Tournament doctor, when
actually ingesting medications. It would be normal for him to rely on the
trustworthiness and knowledge of the Tournament doctor if the doctor handed
the medications to him, but any professional athlete these days has to be wary
when, as in this case, he receives medications which, he knows, have gone
through several hands. Thus, the player cannot establish that he bears No Fault
or Negligence for the Doping Offense. What is determinative of the level of fault
or negligence is not only what the player actually knew or expected but also
what he could have suspected.”3;
- The above-mentioned principle was further confirmed in the case CAS
2011/A/2512 (WADA v. FIS & Kontinen) and the case CAS 2006/A/1025
Mariano Puerta v. International Tennis Federation (ITF), both of which did
echo and rely on the same principle that an athlete must exercise “utmost
caution” with respect to substances ingested and that loss of control, lack
of safeguards, or unattended exposure undermines any claim of “No Fault
or Negligence” (confirming at the same time that athletes can benefit in
those cases from No Significant Fault or Negligence provision);
3 CAS 2005/A/951, Canas v. ATP, page 1, available at: https://jurisprudence.tas-cas.org/pdf/951.pdf
6

- The FEI furthermore noted that although Trazodone was listed as a
Banned Substance under the 2025 FEI Prohibited Substance List, there
were changes made to the 2026 FEI Prohibited Substance List4 and
Trazodone is classified currently as a Controlled Medication;
- According to article 24.2.2 “Any EAD Rule violation case which is pending as
of the Effective Date and any EAD Rule violation case brought after the Effective
Date based on an EAD Rule violation which occurred prior to the Effective Date,
shall be governed by the substantive EAD Rule in effect at the time the alleged
EAD Rule violation occurred, and not by the substantive EAD Rule set out in
these EAD Rules, unless the panel hearing the case determines the principle of
“lex mitior” appropriately applies under the circumstances of the case.”;
- As Trazodone cases are currently prosecuted under the Controlled
Medication Rules for which the maximum sanction is 6 months of
ineligibility (or even an Administrative Procedure, if it is a first violation for
the PR and the Horse), the FEI submits that indeed lex mitior is applicable
to the current proceedings and the fairness requires that the ineligibility
period applicable to the current matter be assessed accordingly;
- Given the overall circumstances of the case at hand, the FEI agreed that
the PR bore No Significant Fault or Negligence for her EADCMR rule
violation and her level of Fault/Negligence falls in the lower range of the
applicable sanction.
16. For the reasons stated above, the FEI concluded that the PR established that she
bore No Significant Fault or Negligence for the EAD rule violation and the period of
ineligibly should therefore be reduced in accordance with the Article 10.6.1.2
EADCMR and lex mitior principle and shall amount to two (2) months ineligibility
period.
17. In accordance with the Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADR, the FEI confirmed that
results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified, with all
resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and
prizes, regardless of the level of fault.
18. The FEI also noted that lex mitior principle should be applied to the fine imposed on
the PR and should therefore amount to 1’500 CHF in accordance with the FEI
Guidelines for Fines and Contributions Towards Legal Costs5 applicable to the
4 2026 FEI Equine Prohibited Substances List.
https://inside.fei.org/sites/default/files/2026%20Prohibited%20Substances%20List.pdf
5 FEI Guidelines for Fines and Contributions towards Legal Costs, effective as of 1 January 2025, available at:
https://inside.fei.org/sites/default/files/FEI_Guidelines_Legal_Costs%20-%20Final%20-
%20Effective%20as%20of%201%20January%202025.pdf
7

Controlled Medication violations. Finally, as the case was concluded with a
Settlement Agreement the FEI does not seek any contribution to the legal costs.
19. On 23 March 2026 January 2026, the FEI notified the Tribunal that it had reached a
settlement of the dispute with the PR, which included the reduction of the period of
Ineligibility to be imposed on the PR.
20. On 1 April 2026, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a one-
person hearing panel (the “Hearing Panel”) to adjudicate and approve this case. The
Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the Hearing
Panel by 6 April 2026.
21. On 2 April 2026, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of the
Hearing Panel.
22. The PR did not submit any objection to the constitution of the Hearing Panel.
IV. Accepted Terms
23. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EAD
Rules and is subject to the approval of the Tribunal. Article 10.8.2 of the EADR
permits for an agreement between the parties, subject to the FEI Tribunal’s
approval.
24. In the matter of the Adverse Analytical Finding related to the samples, which were
collected from the PR’s Horse P G WITHERNAY in the CCI3*-L - Hartpury (GBR), held
between 5 and 10 August 2025, the PR and the FEI agree in accordance with the
Article 10.8.2 of the EADR on the following:
a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 EADR (The presence of a Banned
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample);
b) The PR established on a balance of probabilities how Trazodone entered the
Horse’s system;
c) The PR established that she bore No Significant Fault or Negligence for the
rule violation in accordance with Article 10.6.1.2 EADCMR and the period of
Ineligibility imposed on the PR shall amount to two (2) months of
suspension, commencing as of the date of the final FEI Tribunal Decision
(the Provisional Suspension served by the PR shall be credited against the
imposed period of Ineligibility);
8

d) The results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified,
with all resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals,
points and prizes, in accordance with Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADRs;
e) The PR shall pay a fine of 1’500 CHF;
f) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection
with these proceedings;
g) No other Sanctions will apply in this case;
h) This violation of the EADCMRs shall be considered a prior violation for the
purpose of Multiple Violations in accordance with Article 10.9 of the
EADCMRs.
25. This agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and is subject
to the approval of the FEI Tribunal. The Parties hereby kindly request that the FEI
Tribunal issue a Decision incorporating the terms of this agreement.
26. In accordance with the Article 10.8.2 of the EADR, the Decision by the FEI to enter
or not enter into a case resolution agreement, and the amount of the reduction to,
and the starting date of, the period of Ineligibility and the confirmation of the case
resolution agreement by the FEI Tribunal are not subject to appeal under Article 13
of the EADR.
27. The parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADR, the
Decision will be made public by the FEI.
28. The terms set out in the agreement have been agreed as a full and final settlement
of all claims relating to the subject-matter of these proceedings. Accordingly, any
and all other claims for relief that any party might otherwise have made against
another in relation to the subject-matter of these proceedings are released and
discharged unconditionally, and they may not be pursued in any form hereafter.
V. Decision
29. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes,
Article 159 of the GRs, the EADCMR Rules, the VRs and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR
is a member of the GBR-NF, which is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound
by the EADRs.
30. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement
9

and the Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel takes note that the FEI has agreed that
the PR established, on a balance of probabilities, how Trazodone entered the
Horse’s system.
31. The Hearing Panel further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on
the terms to conclude these proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the
EAD Rules, as detailed under Section IV of this Final Decision.
32. The Hearing Panel confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement
comply with the EAD Rules and finds no grounds to object to them.
33. In particular, the Hearing Panel notes that, in view of the Settlement Agreement
reached by the parties that the PR bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for the
EAD Rule Violation, the period of Ineligibility imposed on the PR is reduced to a
period of two months, starting as at the date of the Provisional Suspension.
34. Therefore, and in accordance with the mutual consent of the Parties, the Hearing
Panel hereby directs the Parties to fully comply with all the terms of the Settlement
Agreement. Furthermore, this Final Decision concludes this case, C26-0006
ROBINSON, 2025/BS09 P G WITHERNAY
35. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 13.3 of the EAD Rules,
this Final Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the Settlement
Agreement are full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject matter
of these proceedings.
36. The Settlement Agreement and this Final Decision are not subject to appeal under
Article 12 of the EAD Rules.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
b. The Secretary General of the NF of the person sanctioned: Yes
c. Any other: No
FOR THE FEI TRIBUNAL
______________________________________________________________________
Ms Diane Pitts, One-Member Panel
